To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the p-block elements As, Ge, Si, Ga, P and Al can segregate from Mg to surfaces of transition metal impurity particles, reduce H adsorption and hence HER on these surfaces, and hence increase the corrosion resistance of Mg alloys.

the six p-block alloying elements (As, Ge, Si, Ga, P, and Al) can inhibit the HER on Fe particles and reduce Mg alloy corrosion, while the same elements are not effective in inhibiting the HER on Ni particles, and the HER on Cu particles is inhibited only by Al.

(i) As and Ge are predicted to be effective in reducing Mg corrosion via their ability to inhibit HER on Fe surfaces, (ii) six p-block elements (As, Ge, Si, Ga, P and Al) meet the criteria for HER inhibition on Fe surfaces, and (iii) As and Ge also have the potential to inhibit HER on Ni surfaces, but not on Cu surfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying elements that can inhibit Mg corrosion and the underlying mechanisms of their action, which is a significant advance in Mg alloy design.

the development of computational tools to design Mg alloys with built-in corrosion protection, and the first application of this approach is to identify p-block alloying elements that can reduce the rate of the cathodic HER on Fe second-phase particles in order to improve corrosion resistance.
a first-principles search of the periodic table for alloying elements in Mg alloys with Fe second-phase particles that can increase corrosion resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the six p-block alloying elements (As, Ge, Si, Ga, P, and Al) are predicted to inhibit Mg corrosion by impeding the cathodic HER on Fe second-phase particles.
the six elements predicted to be corrosion inhibiting in this study, namely As, Ge, Si, Ga, P, and Al, can be considered as potential corrosion-inhibiting alloying elements to be tested in Mg alloys.
As and Ge are promising corrosion-inhibiting elements, but that the six p-block alloying elements identified here are also promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HER is reduced on Fe surfaces of Mg alloys by the segregation of p-block elements to these surfaces and the resulting Pauli repulsion between their orbitals and those of H adsorbate.
the six p-block alloying elements identified here can be used to reduce HER on second-phase particles of Fe and Ni in Mg, but not Cu.
the p-block elements are promising alloying elements for Mg alloys that have second-phase particles of Fe, Ni or Mn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high-throughput calculations can provide a rational basis for designing Mg alloy systems that are inherently corrosion-resistant.
high-throughput calculations can be used to design Mg alloys with built-in corrosion protection by alloying elements that can inhibit the HER on Fe-rich second-phase particles.
a computational search can identify alloying elements that inhibit corrosion of Mg via their ability to reduce HER on second-phase particles.
